| `dapc` | Dual cross-modulated Atari Punk Console: two `apc` nodes feed each other's frequency (`fm`) and width (`width_mod`) at audio rate, so each pulse train shapes the other. `ratio1`/`ratio2` tune the two astables (note-derived Q16 ratios), `width1`/`width2` are the monostable widths (Q16 samples, absolute time), and `xf12`/`xw12`/`xf21`/`xw21` are the four cross-mod depths (Q15, unity = full). The two outputs sum through `level` and a `dc_block` removes the pulse DC. Each cross-mod path has a `delay1` breaker so the graph cycle resolves; the modulation is therefore one sample late (standard audio-rate feedback). Set the depths below unity for subtle chaos, at unity for the full aggressive DAPC. | — | `out`(audio) | `level` → `lvl.level`, `ratio1` → `a1.inc_ratio`, `ratio2` → `a2.inc_ratio`, `width1` → `a1.width`, `width2` → `a2.width`, `xf12` → `g12.level`, `xf21` → `g21.level`, `xw12` → `w12.level`, `xw21` → `w21.level` |

| `va_osc` | Virtual analogue oscillator: tuned_phasor → phase_dist (d-only, PWM) → naive_osc. `shape` (0 = band-limited saw, 1 = sine, 2 = triangle, 3 = band-limited pulse, 4 = white noise); `octave` (−3..3), `semi` (−11..11), `cent` (−100..100) tune the pitch (note-derived); `width` is the phase_dist bend `d` — 16384 (default) = no bend, anything else phase-distorts the tonal shapes (classic PWM on the pulse, a bent timbre on saw/sine/triangle); `width_mod` wires a control source into the bend. Saw and pulse are band-limited (six levels via `mip`), noise ignores pitch. | `fm`(audio), `pitch`(control), `width_mod`(control) | `audio`(audio) | `cent` → `ph.cent`, `octave` → `ph.octave`, `semi` → `ph.semi`, `shape` → `osc.shape`, `width` → `pd.d` |
